h1: Wellness Devicex — Health Landing Page Design
tagline: Landing page reference built on black #0A0A0A and muted blue #64748B, set in Inter and measured against 100vh sections.
summary: Landing page reference for a health or wellbeing product — Inter, cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.18, 1) easing, glass panels and 60ms transitions.
about: Wellness Devicex was captured at 1460x1080 and kept as a specification rather than as a gallery image. Colour is limited to black #0A0A0A underneath and muted blue #64748B carrying the accents, set in Inter. The reference is built with React and Tailwind CSS, and the layout decisions are stated independently of it. Motion is 60ms transitions, cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.18, 1) and a looping video bed, kept quiet enough that the copy still leads. It is the right reference for a health or wellbeing product landing page that has to look deliberate on the first screen.

layout.title: Links collapse at one width
layout.body: The bar carries the wordmark, the section links and one #64748B button, measured at 100vh sections and 24px spacing steps so it never grows into a second header. The links are set below the wordmark in size, and the #64748B action is the only element in the bar with any weight.

layout.title: The loop is the backdrop
layout.body: The first screen is a single clip at 1460x1080, and everything else is arranged on top of it. Export at 1460x1080 or wider and the cover crop keeps working. Export at 1460x1080 or wider to keep the crop honest.

layout.title: Tracking tightens as it grows
layout.body: With Inter doing the work, the sizes step down hard from the headline to the supporting copy and letter-spacing tightens as the size grows, so the hierarchy is carried by type rather than colour. Numerals share the interface face, so statistics and labels belong to the same system.

layout.title: Navigation held to one row
layout.body: If your own page has more sections, group them rather than widening the bar. The reference was captured at 1460x1080.

motion.title: Fast enough to feel deliberate
motion.body: The brief fixes the transition value at 60ms, so a rebuild cannot substitute a slower default. The quoted timing covers state changes, so the feedback is the part of the motion that is specified. Fast state changes, no scroll timelines.

motion.title: The page assembles as you move
motion.body: Parallax runs while the page is moving, so the composition has a defined resting state. Because it is tied to position, the effect resolves the same way on every visit. Never gate the copy behind a scroll trigger.

editorial.title: How the landing page reflows
editorial.body: A fluid scale and a stepped one look similar on a wide screen. Narrow the viewport and the difference shows: a clamp between 48px and 24px against fixed jumps. The order is the last thing to change.

editorial.title: What to change first in Wellness Devicex
editorial.body: The brief names Inter and the scale beside it. Substitute a face with the same proportions and the composition survives. The composition is the reusable part, and it survives a different brand.

editorial.title: How Wellness Devicex sequences the first read
editorial.body: A strict order costs you flexibility later. Add a section above the fold and 100vh sections and 24px spacing steps have to be re-cut, because the sequence is load-bearing rather than decorative. A health reader gets the offer before the options.

faq.question: What does the brief behind Wellness Devicex actually contain?
faq.answer: The captured brief runs 6,903 characters and covers the frame, the type scale, the palette and the transitions. Copying it gives you that text, and sending it to Studio stages the same request with the page already described.

faq.question: Why does the entry name React and Tailwind CSS at all?
faq.answer: Wellness Devicex was built in React and Tailwind CSS, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

faq.question: Can I keep the Wellness Devicex transitions and change the timings?
faq.answer: Entrances and state changes are in the 60ms range on cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.18, 1). They are driven by state changes rather than a scroll library, and they never hold up the copy.

audience: If the motion has to be dropped, the landing page still reads, with 100vh sections and 24px spacing steps doing the hierarchy work.
Product marketers who need the landing page to still read with 4.4s of looping video behind the copy.
